[...] In 2014, ecologists were alerted to similar rings of vegetation outside Africa, in a part of the Pilbara in Western Australia. [...] Studies show that these circles pass through a life cycle of some 30 to 60 years. [...] In 2013, this theory was supported by Norbert Juergens. [...] The sand termite was found in 80-100% of the circles, in 100% of newly formed circles [...] Sand termites create the fairy circle by consuming vegetation and burrowing in the soil to create the ring. The barren circle allows water to percolate down through sandy soil and accumulate underground [...] remarked that Juergens "has made the common scientific error of confusing correlation (even very strong correlation) with causation". [...] "We have not found such a ubiquitous presence of sand termites at fairy circles as was suggested by Juergens [2013] when carrying out ad hoc searches throughout the fairy circle range." [...] They examined the conditions under which fairy circles arise and found that fairy circles are negatively correlated with precipitation and soil nutrition. This observation is consistent with resource competition being a cause of the circles. [...] In May 2014, Getzin et al. demonstrated that termite or gas activity cannot explain the extremely regular spacing of the fairy circles, but the patterns are congruent with typical patterns resulting from vegetation self-organization. [...] The spatially periodic (Turing-like) pattern of fairy circles is a typical example of vegetation self-organization in desert regions. [...] In 2022, a study was published that tested the termite theory and the theory of plant self-organization for Namibia by excavating hundreds of grasses within and around the fairy circles. The study revealed that the grasses within fairy circles died of plant-water stress but not due to root herbivory by termites because the roots were initially undamaged [...] In February 2025, Cramer and Tschinkel published a review article about all fairy circle theories. They emphasize that the self-organization of vegetation is the only theory that is consistent with all field observations [...] the Himba people note that their original ancestor, Mukuru, was responsible for the creation of the fairy circles, or that they were the footprints of gods. [...] In some cases, fairy circles have disappeared within a span of 10 years or less, while other fairy circles may have lasted for centuries. [...] Later in 2013, Michael Cramer and Nichole Barger suggested that the circles were the consequence of vegetation patterns that arose naturally from competition between grasses. [...] According to Walter Tschinkel, this theory accounts for all the characteristics of fairy circles

gancho: O romanesco, a couve-flor verde em espirais pontudas, é quase um fractal. Um estudo de 2021 explicou: seus brotos tentam virar flores, falham, viram ramos que tentam de novo, numa reação em cadeia.
explicacao: No romanesco, cada botão é feito de botões menores, também arranjados em espiral logarítmica, e o desenho se repete em escalas cada vez menores, até que o detalhe fica pequeno demais e a repetição para. Por isso ele é só aproximadamente um fractal. O número de espirais na cabeça é um número de Fibonacci. Pesquisadores do CNRS e do Inria, na França, combinaram biologia de plantas e modelos matemáticos e publicaram a explicação na Science, em julho de 2021. Os botões da couve-flor nascem programados para virar flores, mas nunca chegam lá: viram caules, que continuam tentando produzir flores, e o resultado é uma sucessão de caules sobre caules. A breve passagem pelo estado de flor muda o funcionamento desses brotos, que crescem sem folhas e se multiplicam quase sem fim. O que distingue o romanesco é a aceleração: seus caules produzem novos botões cada vez mais rápido, enquanto nas outras couves-flores o ritmo é constante, e isso dá a cada florete a forma de pirâmide. Segundo os autores, é um exemplo de como mutações escolhidas na domesticação mudaram a forma das hortaliças.

fontes.titulo: Where does the shape of the Romanesco cauliflower come from? (CNRS)
fontes.trecho: The mystery of the formation of one of the most peculiar plant forms – the Romanesco cauliflower – has been solved by a team of scientists from the CNRS1 and Inria in an article published on the 9 July in Science. Thanks to work combining mathematical modelling and plant biology, the scientists were able to determine that cauliflowers, and Romanescos in particular, are in fact buds that are designed to become flowers but which never reach their goal. Instead, they develop into stems, which in turn continue trying to produce flowers. The cauliflower is born from this chain reaction, resulting in a succession of stems upon stems. This study shows that the brief incursion of buds into a flowering state profoundly affects their functioning and allows them, unlike normal stems, to grow without leaves and to multiply almost infinitely. The atypical shape of the Romanesco is explained by the fact that its stems produce buds more and more rapidly (whereas the production rate is constant in other cauliflowers). This acceleration gives each floret a pyramidal appearance, making the fractal aspect of the structure clear. The study highlights how the selection of mutations in plants during the process of domestication has changed their shape [...] Science, 9 July 2021.

each bud is composed of a series of smaller buds, all arranged in yet another logarithmic spiral. This self-similar pattern continues at smaller levels. The pattern is only an approximate fractal since the pattern eventually terminates when the feature size becomes sufficiently small. The number of spirals on the head of Romanesco broccoli is a Fibonacci number.

gancho: Quem é atingido por raio pode ganhar na pele um desenho ramificado, como uma samambaia, que costuma sumir em 24 horas. É uma figura de Lichtenberg, padrão fractal estudado em 1777, num experimento que antecipou a xerox.
explicacao: O físico alemão Georg Christoph Lichtenberg construiu em 1777 um grande eletróforo, aparelho que gera eletricidade estática de alta tensão. Depois de descarregar uma ponta eletrizada sobre uma placa isolante, ele polvilhava pós sobre ela, e os grãos grudavam nas áreas carregadas, revelando desenhos radiais e ramificados. Ao pressionar folhas de papel sobre esses desenhos, conseguia transferi-los e guardá-los, o princípio básico da xerografia moderna. Os padrões têm propriedades fractais e costumam surgir quando uma descarga elétrica rompe um material isolante, seja sólido, líquido ou gás. Um raio pode gravar uma figura assim na grama em volta do ponto atingido, às vezes em campos de golfe. Na pele das vítimas de raio, as marcas também são chamadas de marcas queraunográficas. Para os engenheiros, elas são um sinal de alerta: as "árvores elétricas" que crescem dentro de isolantes acompanham a deterioração de equipamentos de alta tensão.

fontes.trecho: A Lichtenberg figure (German: Lichtenberg-Figur), or Lichtenberg dust figure, is a branching electric discharge that sometimes appears on the surface or in the interior of insulating materials. Lichtenberg figures are often associated with the progressive deterioration of high-voltage components and equipment. [...] Lichtenberg figures are now known to occur on or within solids, liquids, and gases during electrical breakdown. Lichtenberg figures are natural phenomena that exhibit fractal properties. [...] Lichtenberg figures are named after the German physicist Georg Christoph Lichtenberg, who originally discovered and studied them. [...] In 1777, Lichtenberg built a large electrophorus to generate high-voltage static electricity through induction. After discharging a high-voltage point to the surface of an insulator, he recorded the resulting radial patterns by sprinkling various powdered materials onto the surface. By then pressing blank sheets of paper onto these patterns, Lichtenberg was able to transfer and record these images, thereby discovering the basic principle of modern xerography. [...] Lichtenberg figures are fern-like patterns that may appear on the skin of lightning strike victims and typically disappear in 24 hours. They are also known as Keraunographic markings. A lightning strike can also create a large Lichtenberg figure in grass surrounding the point struck. These are sometimes found on golf courses or in grassy meadows.

gancho: A Calçada dos Gigantes, na Irlanda do Norte, tem cerca de 40 mil colunas de basalto, a maioria com seis lados. Ninguém as esculpiu: a lava rachou ao esfriar. Amido de milho secando faz colunas parecidas, em miniatura.
explicacao: As colunas nasceram de uma erupção vulcânica há cerca de 60 milhões de anos, e a lenda local diz que o gigante Finn McCool construiu a calçada para chegar à Escócia. A física é outra. Ao esfriar, a lava solidificada se contrai e precisa rachar para aliviar a tensão. As primeiras rachaduras, na superfície, se encontram em forma de T, como na lama seca, porque cada uma corre até topar com outra. Mas a frente de rachaduras vai descendo pela rocha, e a cada avanço o desenho se reorganiza num arranjo de menor energia. Alguns metros abaixo, já virou uma grade de hexágonos de largura parecida. A largura depende do material e da velocidade da frente, controlada pela água subterrânea. Como todas as colunas desse tipo seguem uma proporção parecida entre largura, velocidade e difusão do calor, dá para fazer um modelo em escala: uma camada de amido de milho de 1 cm, ao secar, forma colunas de cerca de 1 mm. Na Calçada, há colunas de quatro a oito lados, e as mais altas têm uns 12 metros.

fontes.trecho: Columnar jointing occurs in many types of igneous rocks (e.g. basalt, andesite, rhyolite, tuff), and forms as the rock cools and contracts. [...] As it cools down further, the basalt contracts, and it forms cracks to release the tensile energy. It then is cooled down further by groundwater boiling and reflux. When the cracks first form at the surface, the cracks are dominated by T-junctions, like mudcracks, because they were formed individually. One crack would form and move across the surface, until it hits upon a previous crack, forming a T-junction. Then, these cracks extend downwards in a moving front that is roughly planar and parallel to the surface. As it moves, the crack pattern anneals to become lower in energy. The speed v at which the front moves is determined by the groundwater flow rate. After the front moves a few meters deep, it would evolve into a hexagonal grid with roughly equal width L. The width L is determined by the basalt's material properties, and the speed v at which the front moves. [...] For all columnar jointing, the value of Pe is around 0.2, and thus the shape and speed of all columnar joints are similar after scaling. A scaled model can be made by drying cornstarch a centimeter thick, which creates columns about 1 mm wide. [...] The Giant's Causeway (Irish: Clochán An Aifir) on the north Antrim coast of Northern Ireland was created by volcanic activity 60 million years ago, and consists of over 40,000 columns. According to a legend, the giant Finn McCool created the Giant's Causeway, as a causeway to Scotland. [...] For basalt, Pe≈0.35. For cornstarch, Pe≈0.1.

is an area of approximately 40,000 interlocking basalt columns, the result of an ancient volcanic fissure eruption [...] Most of the columns are hexagonal, although some have between four and eight sides. The tallest are approximately 12 metres (39 ft) high

gancho: Numa região arenosa da Flórida, onde os vales são cavados pela água que brota do chão, os riachos se dividem num ângulo médio de 72 graus. Foi o que uma teoria do MIT previu, e quase 5 mil bifurcações confirmaram.
explicacao: Lá, a erosão não vem de enxurradas na superfície, e sim da água subterrânea. Guardada nos morros em volta, ela escorre devagar pela areia porosa, aflora na cabeceira do vale e leva grãos junto. Com o tempo, isso alonga o vale até ele se partir em dois. A equipe do geofísico Dan Rothman calculou os caminhos da água subterrânea em direção a dois riachos recém-separados. Quando o ângulo entre eles é pequeno, esses caminhos se curvam para longe um do outro; quando é grande, se curvam um para o outro. Só num ângulo especial, 72 graus, eles seguem retos, e o grupo concluiu que é nesse ângulo que os riachos se dividem. A previsão foi testada em quase 5 mil junções de riachos no Panhandle da Flórida, perto da cidade de Bristol, e a média bateu com o número. O artigo saiu em dezembro de 2012 na revista PNAS. Segundo Rothman, a mesma análise talvez sirva para outros sistemas que se ramificam, como os dendritos dos neurônios e os filamentos de fungos.

fontes.trecho: In a paper published this week in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, Dan Rothman and his colleagues formulate a mathematical theory to discover a common angle at which valleys branch. In environments where erosion is driven by the seepage of water out of the ground, the group’s theory predicts that rivers branch at an angle of 72 degrees. Putting the theory to the test, Rothman and his group measured 5,000 branching angles in the Florida Panhandle, a region of soft, sandy soils — finding that the average valley branching was indeed 72 degrees. Rothman, a professor of geophysics in MIT’s Department of Earth, Atmospheric and Planetary Sciences (EAPS), says such a mathematical analysis may also be applicable to other systems, such as neuron dendrites and fungal filaments. [...] Near the town of Bristol, along the eastern stretch of the Florida Panhandle, a network of valleys cuts into the landscape [...] Essentially, groundwater stored in the hills surrounding a valley slowly seeps out, carrying with it some sand. Over time, the process slowly erodes the surrounding hills, extending a valley and eventually splitting it in two. To find the angle at which this split occurs, Rothman’s group derived a mathematical expression for the paths taken by groundwater as it flows toward a newly split stream. Such paths generally curve either away from each other, when the angle between the streams is small, or toward each other, when the angle is large. However, Rothman’s group found that there is a special angle — 72 degrees — for which the paths are straight, reasoning that this is the angle at which streams branch. They subsequently confirmed their prediction by examining nearly 5,000 stream junctions in the Florida Panhandle. [...] Publication Date: December 5, 2012

gancho: Em 1951, o soviético Boris Belousov viu uma mistura química oscilar sozinha entre amarelo e incolor. Revistas recusaram o artigo duas vezes, porque ele não conseguia explicar o fenômeno. Hoje a reação é um clássico.
explicacao: Belousov procurava uma versão sem seres vivos do ciclo de Krebs, parte da respiração das células. Na mistura de bromato de potássio, sulfato de cério, ácidos malônico e cítrico e ácido sulfúrico diluído, o cério alternava entre duas formas, e a cor ia e voltava. Como não convenceu os editores com uma explicação, só conseguiu publicar em 1959, numa revista menos prestigiada e sem revisão por pares. Em 1961, o bioquímico Simon Shnoll passou o problema a um aluno de pós-graduação, Anatol Zhabotinsky, que destrinchou a sequência de reações, mas o trabalho só ficou conhecido no Ocidente numa conferência em Praga, em 1968. A reação mostra que nem toda química corre direto para o equilíbrio. Numa placa de Petri, ela forma pontos coloridos que crescem em anéis concêntricos ou espirais, que somem quando se agita a placa e depois voltam. Espirais muito parecidas aparecem em colônias de uma ameba do solo, o Dictyostelium, só que formadas por células inteiras, e não por moléculas. O mecanismo envolve cerca de 18 etapas.

fontes.trecho: The reactions are important to theoretical chemistry in that they show that chemical reactions do not have to be dominated by equilibrium thermodynamic behavior. [...] The discovery of the phenomenon is credited to Boris Belousov. In 1951, while trying to find the non-organic analog to the Krebs cycle, he noted that in a mix of potassium bromate, cerium(IV) sulfate, malonic acid, and citric acid in dilute sulfuric acid, the ratio of concentration of the cerium(IV) and cerium(III) ions oscillated, causing the colour of the solution to oscillate between a yellow solution and a colorless solution. [...] Belousov made two attempts to publish his finding, but was rejected on the grounds that he could not explain his results to the satisfaction of the editors of the journals to which he submitted his results. [...] In 1959 his work was finally published in a less respectable, nonreviewed journal. After Belousov's publication, Shnoll gave the project in 1961 to a graduate student, Anatol Zhabotinsky, who investigated the reaction sequence in detail; however, the results of these men's work were still not widely disseminated, and were not known in the West until a conference in Prague in 1968. [...] These reactions, if carried out in petri dishes, result in the formation first of colored spots. These spots grow into a series of expanding concentric rings or perhaps expanding spirals [...] The colors disappear if the dishes are shaken, and then reappear. [...] Strikingly similar oscillatory spiral patterns appear elsewhere in nature, at very different spatial and temporal scales, for example the growth pattern of Dictyostelium discoideum, a soil-dwelling amoeba colony. In the BZ reaction, the size of the interacting elements is molecular and the time scale of the reaction is minutes. In the case of the soil amoeba, the size of the elements is typical of single-celled organisms [...] The mechanism for this reaction is very complex and is thought to involve around 18 different steps

gancho: Pi aparece onde ninguém esperava: contando quantos passos um ponto leva para escapar do conjunto de Mandelbrot perto de um gargalo estreito. Com o ponto a 0,0000001 do gargalo, são 31.415.928 passos.
explicacao: O conjunto de Mandelbrot reúne os números complexos c para os quais repetir a conta z → z² + c, começando de zero, nunca dispara para o infinito. Sua borda é infinitamente complicada: tão "enrugada" que, como provou Mitsuhiro Shishikura, tem dimensão fractal 2, a mesma de uma superfície. Para saber se um ponto c = −3/4 + iε, logo acima de um estreitamento da figura, está fora do conjunto, repete-se a conta até o valor sair de um círculo de raio maior que 2. O número de repetições necessárias, multiplicado por ε, se aproxima de pi. Com ε = 0,0000001, são 31.415.928 repetições, e o produto dá 3,1415928. Muita gente fez esse experimento de forma independente no começo dos anos 1990, como David Boll. Algo parecido acontece em outros pontos. Uma prova para c = 1/4 saiu em 2001, e em 2023 um trabalho de graduação explicou por que surge pi ali: é a metade da circunferência de um círculo de raio 1. Em 2025, três estudantes do ensino médio estenderam a explicação a todos os infinitos pontos de bifurcação do conjunto.

fontes.trecho: the complex numbers c for which the function fc(z)=z2+c does not diverge to infinity when iterated starting at z=0. [...] Images of the Mandelbrot set exhibit an infinitely complicated boundary [...] The Hausdorff dimension of the boundary of the Mandelbrot set equals 2 as determined by a result of Mitsuhiro Shishikura. [...] Roughly speaking, Shishikura's result states that the Mandelbrot set boundary is so "wiggly" that it locally fills space as eff [...] There are intriguing experiments in the Mandelbrot set that lead to the occurrence of the number π. For a parameter c=−34+iε with ε>0, verifying that c is not in the Mandelbrot set means iterating the sequence z↦z2+c starting with z=0, until the sequence leaves the disk around 0 of any radius R>2. [...] It turns out that the necessary number of iterations, multiplied by ε, converges to pi. For example, for ε = 0.0000001, and R=2, the number of iterations is 31415928 and the product is 3.1415928. This experiment was performed independently by many people in the early 1990s, if not before; for instance by David Boll. Analogous observations have also been made at the parameters c=−5/4 and c=1/4 (with a necessary modification in the latter case). In 2001, Aaron Klebanoff published a (non-conceptual) proof for this phenomenon at c=1/4 In 2023, Paul Siewert developed, in his Bachelor thesis, a conceptual proof also for the value c=1/4, explaining why the number pi occurs (geometrically as half the circumference of the unit circle). In 2025, the three high school students Thies Brockmöller, Oscar Scherz, and Nedim Srkalovic extended the theory and the conceptual proof to all the infinitely many bifurcation points in the Mandelbrot set.

gancho: No polo norte de Saturno, as nuvens formam um hexágono com lados de cerca de 14.500 km, mais que o diâmetro da Terra, estável há décadas. Num laboratório, um tanque de líquido girando produziu formas parecidas.
explicacao: O hexágono apareceu nas imagens das sondas Voyager, de 1981, e foi revisto pela Cassini a partir de 2006. Tem uns 300 km de altura e pode ser uma corrente de jato com ventos de 320 km/h. Ele gira com período de 10 h 39 min 24 s, o mesmo das emissões de rádio vindas do interior do planeta, e, ao contrário de outras nuvens, não se desloca em longitude. Entre 2012 e 2016, mudou de azulado para dourado, talvez por uma névoa criada pela luz do Sol com a mudança de estação. O polo sul não tem hexágono. Por que seis lados? Ainda há várias hipóteses. Uma, de Oxford, propõe que ele se forme onde a velocidade dos ventos muda bruscamente com a latitude. Num tanque circular com o centro e a borda girando em velocidades diferentes, surgiram polígonos de três a oito lados, sendo o hexágono o mais comum, formados por redemoinhos que se espaçam por igual ao longo da fronteira. Outros pesquisadores contestam que o laboratório mostre o mesmo fenômeno, e há modelos alternativos.

fontes.trecho: Saturn's hexagon is a persistent approximately hexagonal cloud pattern around the north pole of the planet Saturn [...] The sides of the hexagon are about 14,500 km (9,000 mi) long, which is about 2,000 km (1,200 mi) longer than the diameter of Earth. The hexagon is around 300 km (190 mi) high, and may be a jet stream made of atmospheric gases moving at 320 km/h (200 mph). It rotates with a period of 10h 39m 24s, the same period as Saturn's radio emissions from its interior. The hexagon does not shift in longitude like other clouds in the visible atmosphere. Saturn's hexagon was discovered during the Voyager mission in 1981, and was later revisited by Cassini-Huygens in 2006. [...] Saturn's south pole does not have a hexagon [...] Multiple hypotheses for the hexagonal cloud pattern have been developed. [...] Between 2012 and 2016, the hexagon changed from a mostly blue color to more of a golden color. One hypothesis for this is that sunlight is creating haze as the pole is exposed to sunlight due to the change in season. [...] A hypothesis developed at Oxford University is the hexagon forms where there is a steep latitudinal gradient in the speed of the atmospheric winds in Saturn's atmosphere. Similar regular shapes were created in a laboratory when a circular tank of liquid was rotated at different speeds at its centre and periphery. The most common shape was six sided, but shapes with three to eight sides were also produced. [...] A number of stable vortices of similar size form on the slower (south) side of the fluid boundary, and these interact with each other to space themselves out evenly around the perimeter. [...] Other researchers claim that lab studies exhibit vortex streets, a series of spiraling vortices not observed in Saturn's hexagon.

gancho: O floco de neve de seis braços iguais, o dos desenhos, é raro: estudos sugerem que menos de 0,1% dos flocos tem essa forma ideal. E a temperatura muda tudo: alguns graus a mais de frio, e saem agulhas e colunas ocas.
explicacao: A simetria de seis vem da estrutura hexagonal do cristal de gelo: no início, o floco é um hexagonozinho, e cada braço cresce a partir de um canto. Como os seis braços atravessam quase o mesmo ar, com a mesma temperatura e umidade, tendem a crescer parecidos, mas isso não é garantido, e nenhum floco é perfeitamente simétrico. A variedade foi revelada por Wilson Bentley, que fotografou milhares de flocos ao microscópio a partir de 1885, em busca de dois iguais. Ukichiro Nakaya organizou as formas num diagrama de temperatura e umidade. Até −3 °C, os cristais tendem a ser placas finas. Mais frio, até −8 °C, viram colunas ocas, prismas ou agulhas. Perto de −22 °C, voltam a ser placas, muitas vezes com ramificações. Ar supersaturado de umidade dá formas rendadas; ar mais seco, formas compactas. Quanto à frase "não existem dois flocos iguais", é improvável achar dois idênticos na natureza, já que um floco típico tem cerca de 10 quintilhões de moléculas de água, mas flocos quase idênticos já foram cultivados em laboratório.

fontes.trecho: it is unlikely that any two snowflakes are alike due to the estimated 1019 (10 quintillion) water molecules which make up a typical snowflake [...] Snowflakes that look identical, but may vary at the molecular level, have been grown under controlled conditions. Although snowflakes are never perfectly symmetrical, the growth of a non-aggregated snowflake often approximates six-fold radial symmetry, arising from the hexagonal crystalline structure of ice. At that stage, the snowflake has the shape of a minute hexagon. The six "arms" of the snowflake, or dendrites, then grow independently from each of the corners of the hexagon [...] Since the micro-environment (and its changes) are very nearly identical around the snowflake, each arm tends to grow in nearly the same way. However, being in the same micro-environment does not guarantee that each arm grows the same [...] Empirical studies suggest less than 0.1% of snowflakes exhibit the ideal six-fold symmetric shape. [...] Although nearly-identical snowflakes have been made in laboratories, they are very unlikely to be found in nature. Initial attempts to find identical snowflakes by photographing thousands of them with a microscope from 1885 onward by Wilson Alwyn Bentley found the wide variety of snowflakes we know about today. Ukichiro Nakaya developed a crystal morphology diagram, relating crystal shape to the temperature and moisture conditions under which they formed [...] Freezing air down to  −3 °C (27 °F) promotes planar crystals (t [...] In colder air down to −8 °C (18 °F), the crystals form as hollow columns, prisms or needles. In air as cold as −22 °C (−8 °F), shapes become plate-like again, often with branched or dendritic features. [...] Forms below the saturation line trend more towards solid and compact. Crystals formed in supersaturated air trend more towards lacy, delicate and ornate.

gancho: Nos torneios de computador de Robert Axelrod, por volta de 1980, a estratégia mais simples venceu duas vezes: cooperar na primeira jogada e, dali em diante, só repetir o que o rival fez na anterior.
explicacao: Axelrod pediu a outros teóricos dos jogos que mandassem estratégias para o dilema do prisioneiro repetido, em que cada lado escolhe cooperar ou trair a cada rodada. Cada programa enfrentou todos os outros em partidas de 200 rodadas, somando pontos. Venceu o "olho por olho" (tit for tat), inscrito pelo matemático Anatol Rapoport. Os resultados foram publicados e um segundo torneio foi organizado para ver se alguém conseguia superá-lo. Ninguém conseguiu. O curioso é que o olho por olho nunca faz mais pontos que o adversário da vez: no melhor caso, empata. Ganhou acumulando bons segundos lugares contra todo tipo de rival, porque provocava cooperação em vez de tentar explorar. Já as estratégias ardilosas, que faziam deduções complicadas sobre o outro e traíam de vez em quando para ganhar uns pontos a mais, costumavam errar nas deduções e se saíam mal. Axelrod tirou daí algumas lições: nunca ser o primeiro a trair, revidar a traição, voltar a cooperar assim que o outro voltar, não ter inveja do placar alheio e não tentar ser esperto demais. Num artigo escrito com o biólogo W. D. Hamilton, Axelrod levou essas ideias para a cooperação entre seres vivos, de bactérias a primatas, e o trabalho virou referência.

fontes.trecho: The Evolution of Cooperation is a 1984 book written by political scientist Robert Axelrod that expands upon a paper of the same name written by Axelrod and evolutionary biologist W.D. Hamilton. The article's summary addresses the issue in terms of "cooperation in organisms, whether bacteria or primates". [...] Axelrod initially solicited strategies from other game theorists to compete in the first tournament. Each strategy was paired with each other strategy for 200 iterations of a Prisoner's Dilemma game and scored on the total points accumulated through the tournament. The winner was a very simple strategy submitted by Anatol Rapoport called "tit for tat" (TFT) that cooperates on the first move, and subsequently echoes (reciprocates) what the other player did on the previous move. The results of the first tournament were analyzed and published, and a second tournament was held to see if anyone could find a better strategy. TFT won again. [...] In fact, TFT cannot score higher than its partner; at best it can only do "as good as". Yet it won the tournaments by consistently scoring a strong second-place with a variety of partners. [...] "A common problem with these rules is that they used complex methods of making inferences about the other player [strategy] – and these inferences were wrong." [...] Be nice: cooperate, never be the first to defect. Be provocable: return defection for defection, cooperation for cooperation. Don't be envious: focus on maximizing your own 'score', as opposed to ensuring your score is higher than your 'partner's'. Don't be too clever: or, don't try to be tricky.

The strategy was first introduced by Anatol Rapoport in Robert Axelrod's two tournaments, held around 1980. Notably, it was (on both occasions) both the simplest strategy and the most successful in direct competition.

gancho: O dilema do prisioneiro nasceu sem prisioneiros: em 1950, dois matemáticos da RAND puseram dois colegas para jogá-lo cem vezes, e eles cooperaram com frequência. A história da cadeia só veio depois.
explicacao: No jogo, cada participante escolhe cooperar ou trair. Para cada um, isoladamente, trair é a escolha racional, mas, se os dois cooperam, ambos ganham mais. Quem montou o quebra-cabeça foram Merrill Flood e Melvin Dresher, que trabalhavam na RAND Corporation, em 1950. Para testá-lo, convidaram o economista Armen Alchian e o matemático John Williams a disputar cem rodadas, e os dois escolheram cooperar com frequência. Consultado sobre o resultado, John Nash comentou que, quando o jogo se repete, o comportamento racional pode ser diferente do de uma rodada só. A observação antecipou uma ideia central da teoria dos jogos: a cooperação pode surgir em interações repetidas mesmo quando não seria racional num encontro único. O nome e a versão com dois presos interrogados, que tornaram o jogo famoso, vieram mais tarde, com Albert W. Tucker, que expressou as recompensas em anos de prisão. Tucker, aliás, foi o orientador da tese de doutorado do próprio Nash.

fontes.trecho: each of whom can either cooperate for mutual benefit or betray their partner ("defect") for individual gain. The dilemma arises from the fact that while defecting is rational for each agent, cooperation yields a higher payoff for each. The puzzle was designed by Merrill Flood and Melvin Dresher in 1950 during their work at the RAND Corporation. They invited economist Armen Alchian and mathematician John Williams to play a hundred rounds of the game, observing that Alchian and Williams often chose to cooperate. When asked about the results, John Nash remarked that rational behavior in the iterated version of the game can differ from that in a single-round version. This insight anticipated a key result in game theory: cooperation can emerge in repeated interactions, even in situations where it is not rational in a one-off interaction. Albert W. Tucker later named the game the "prisoner's dilemma" by framing the rewards in terms of prison sentences.
The thesis, written under the supervision of doctoral advisor Albert W. Tucker

gancho: Num torneio de dilema do prisioneiro em 2004, uma universidade inscreveu 60 programas que se reconheciam por uma "senha" de jogadas. Uns se deixavam explorar pelos outros, e os três primeiros lugares foram dela.
explicacao: A competição comemorava 20 anos e permitia várias inscrições por equipe, que era avaliada pelo seu melhor jogador. A Universidade de Southampton, na Inglaterra, explorou essas regras. Seus programas usavam as primeiras cinco a dez jogadas de cada partida como uma espécie de aperto de mão secreto. Quando dois deles se reconheciam, um passava a cooperar sempre e o outro a trair sempre, o que dava ao traidor o máximo de pontos possível. Quando o adversário era de fora, o programa de Southampton traía sem parar, só para baixar a pontuação do rival. Resultado: estratégias da universidade ficaram nos três primeiros lugares, e várias outras perto do fim da tabela, embora as vencedoras tivessem menos vitórias e muito mais derrotas que a estratégia GRIM. Anos antes, Richard Dawkins já tinha apontado, no livro O Gene Egoísta, que estratégias assim poderiam vencer se fossem permitidas várias inscrições. A "dança de dez jogadas" também driblava a proibição de comunicação entre os jogadores, e mostrou quanto a comunicação pode mudar o equilíbrio de um jogo.

fontes.trecho: a team from Southampton University in England introduced a more successful strategy at the 20th-anniversary iterated prisoner's dilemma competition. It relied on collusion between programs to achieve the highest number of points for a single program. The university submitted 60 programs to the competition, which were designed to recognize each other through a series of five to ten moves at the start. Once this recognition was made, one program would always cooperate and the other would always defect, assuring the maximum number of points for the defector. If the program realized that it was playing a non-Southampton player, it would continuously defect in an attempt to minimize the competing program's score. As a result, the 2004 Prisoners' Dilemma Tournament results show University of Southampton's strategies in the first three places (and a number of positions towards the bottom), despite having fewer wins and many more losses than the GRIM strategy. The Southampton strategy takes advantage of the fact that multiple entries were allowed in this particular competition and that a team's performance was measured by that of the highest-scoring player [...] Richard Dawkins, in his book The Selfish Gene, pointed out the possibility of such strategies winning if multiple entries were allowed [...] Such strategies also circumvent the rule against communication between players: the Southampton programs' "ten-move dance" allowed them to recognize one another, reinforcing how valuable communication can be in shifting the balance of the game.

gancho: John Nash ganhou o Nobel de Economia de 1994 por ideias de uma tese de doutorado de 28 páginas. Segundo sua biógrafa, ao mostrar o resultado a von Neumann, ouviu: "Isso é trivial. É só um teorema do ponto fixo."
explicacao: A tese, de 1950, foi orientada por Albert W. Tucker, em Princeton, e trazia a definição do que hoje se chama equilíbrio de Nash: uma situação em que nenhum jogador ganha mais mudando sozinho de estratégia, com as dos outros fixas. Von Neumann e Oskar Morgenstern, no livro de 1944 que deu forma à teoria dos jogos, já tinham mostrado que existe equilíbrio em estratégias mistas (sortear entre opções com certas probabilidades), mas só para jogos de soma zero, em que o ganho de um é a perda do outro. Nash foi muito além: provou que todo jogo com um número finito de ações tem pelo menos um equilíbrio, talvez em estratégias mistas. Para isso, usou teoremas do ponto fixo, os de Brouwer e de Kakutani. Segundo a biografia escrita por Sylvia Nasar (Uma Mente Brilhante), foi em 1949, ao ouvir a ideia, que von Neumann a despachou com essa frase. A ideia de equilíbrio já tinha aparecido num caso particular em 1838, quando Antoine Augustin Cournot analisou empresas que escolhem quanto produzir, mas sem uma definição geral. O Nobel de 1994, dividido com John Harsanyi e Reinhard Selten, premiou o trabalho que Nash fez como aluno de pós-graduação.

fontes.trecho: Nash earned a PhD in 1950 with a 28-page dissertation on noncooperative games. The thesis, written under the supervision of doctoral advisor Albert W. Tucker, contained the definition and properties of the Nash equilibrium, a crucial concept in noncooperative games. [...] In 1994, he received the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences (along with John Harsanyi and Reinhard Selten) for his game theory work as a Princeton graduate student.

In game theory, a Nash equilibrium is a situation where no player could gain more by changing their own strategy (holding all other players' strategies fixed) in a game. [...] The same idea was used in a particular application in 1838 by Antoine Augustin Cournot in his theory of oligopoly. In Cournot's theory, each of several firms choose how much output to produce to maximize its profit. [...] Cournot did not use the idea in any other applications, however, or define it generally. [...] The concept of a mixed-strategy equilibrium was introduced by John von Neumann and Oskar Morgenstern in their 1944 book The Theory of Games and Economic Behavior, but their analysis was restricted to the special case of zero-sum games. [...] The contribution of Nash in his 1951 article "Non-Cooperative Games" was to define a mixed-strategy Nash equilibrium for any game with a finite set of actions and prove that at least one (mixed-strategy) Nash equilibrium must exist in such a game. [...] allowed Nash to employ the Kakutani fixed-point theorem in his 1950 paper to prove existence of equilibria. His 1951 paper used the simpler Brouwer fixed-point theorem for the same purpose. [...] When Nash made this point to John von Neumann in 1949, von Neumann famously dismissed it with the words, "That's trivial, you know. That's just a fixed-point theorem." (See Nasar, 1998, p. 94.)

gancho: Nas trincheiras da Primeira Guerra, inimigos paravam de atirar, às vezes sem combinar nada, ou disparavam de um jeito ritual, sem intenção de matar. Alguns generais chegavam a analisar as baixas para flagrar isso.
explicacao: O fenômeno ganhou o nome de "viva e deixe viver" e surgiu espontaneamente, sobretudo nos longos períodos de guerra de trincheiras na Frente Ocidental. Às vezes eram pactos explícitos, combinados entre os próprios soldados. Em outras, era um acordo mudo: os dois lados evitavam disparar, ou atiravam sempre do mesmo jeito rotineiro, como sinal de que não havia intenção letal. Acontecia entre pequenas unidades, de sentinelas que se recusavam a atirar em inimigos expostos até atiradores de elite, metralhadoras e baterias de artilharia. O exemplo mais famoso é a trégua de Natal de 1914. Os comandos superiores sabiam dessa tendência e, às vezes, analisavam os números de baixas para detectá-la. Para manter o "espírito ofensivo", mandavam fazer incursões e patrulhas, e o sistema, frágil, se desfazia facilmente quando havia mortes. O cientista político Robert Axelrod descreveu o caso como um dilema do prisioneiro repetido: os mesmos soldados se enfrentavam dia após dia, e a cooperação era sustentada pela ameaça de revide, como na estratégia do olho por olho. A leitura é contestada: os cientistas políticos Joanne Gowa e Andrew Gelman argumentaram que as premissas do dilema não valem nesse caso.

fontes.titulo: Live and let live (World War I)
fontes.trecho: Live and let live is the non-aggressive co-operative behavior that developed spontaneously during the First World War, particularly during prolonged periods of trench warfare on the Western Front. Perhaps one of the most famous examples of this is the Christmas truce of 1914. [...] Sometimes it can take the form of overt truces or pacts negotiated locally by soldiers. At other times it can be a tacit behaviour—sometimes characterised as "letting sleeping dogs lie"—whereby both sides refrain from firing or using their weapons, or deliberately discharge them in a ritualistic or routine way that signals their non-lethal intent. [...] This behaviour was found at the small-unit level, sections, platoons or companies [...] Examples were found from the lone soldier standing sentry duty, refusing to fire on exposed enemy soldiers, up to snipers, machine-guns teams and even field-artillery batteries. Upper echelon commanders—those of divisions, corps and armies—and their staffs were aware of this tendency towards non-aggression, and would sometimes analyse casualty statistics to detect it. Raids or patrols were often ordered to foster the correct "offensive spirit" in the troops. The Live and Let Live system was fragile at best and was easily broken by occurrences of lethal force [...] Some scholars of game theory, like Robert Axelrod, have characterised Live and Let Live as an iterated variant of the prisoner's dilemma. Axelrod linked Live and Let Live to the co-operative strategy referred to as Tit for Tat. Axelrod's interpretation of "Live and Let Live" as a prisoner's dilemma has been disputed by political scientists Joanne Gowa and Andrew Gelman, who (separately) argue that the assumptions underlying the prisoner's dilemma do not hold in this example.

gancho: No leilão do dólar, criado pelo economista Martin Shubik, uma nota de 1 dólar vai para o maior lance, mas o segundo colocado também paga o que ofereceu. Lance a lance, os rivais acabam passando de 1 dólar.
explicacao: O jogo mostra como uma sequência de decisões que parecem sensatas no curto prazo leva a um resultado irracional. Quem abre com 5 centavos espera lucrar 95. Mas outro pode oferecer 10 e ainda lucrar 90, e assim por diante. O detalhe cruel é que o segundo colocado perde o que ofereceu, então, a cada lance, quem está atrás prefere subir 5 centavos a pagar por nada. Quando um oferece 95 centavos e o outro chega a 1 dólar, o de 95 tem duas opções: desistir e perder 95 centavos, ou oferecer 1,05 dólar e perder só 5. Subir parece racional, e o processo continua acima do valor da nota, sempre com o segundo colocado perdendo mais que o primeiro. A partir de 1 dólar, só o leiloeiro sai ganhando. Na análise matemática, o que já foi gasto é custo afundado e não deveria pesar na decisão, e o jogo tem parentesco com a "guerra de atrito". Shubik publicou o jogo em 1971 como um paradoxo do comportamento não cooperativo e da escalada.

fontes.trecho: The dollar auction is a non-zero sum sequential game explored by economist Martin Shubik to illustrate how a short-sighted approach to rational choice can lead to decisions that are, in the long-run, irrational. [...] The setup involves an auctioneer who volunteers to auction off a dollar bill with the following rule: the bill goes to the winner; however, the second-highest bidder also loses the amount that they bid, making them the biggest loser in the auction. The winner can get a dollar for a mere 5 cents (the minimum bid), but only if no one else enters into the bidding war. [...] For instance, a player might begin by bidding 5 cents, hoping to make a 95-cent profit. They can be outbid by another player bidding 10 cents, as a 90-cent profit is still desirable. [...] Every player has a choice of either paying for nothing or bidding 5 cents more on the dollar. A series of short-term rational bids will reach and ultimately surpass one dollar as the bidders seek to minimize their losses. If the first bidder bids 95 cents, and the second bidder bids one dollar (for no net gain or loss), the first bidder stands to lose 95 cents unless they bid $1.05, in which case bidding more than the value of the dollar would reduce their losses to only 5 cents. Bidding continues with the second highest bidder always losing more than the highest bidder and therefore always trying to become the high bidder. Once the highest bid reaches one dollar, only the auctioneer will profit in the end. [...] a discrete version of the war of attrition. [...] this follows from the fact that past bids are a sunk cost. [...] Shubik, Martin (1971). "The Dollar Auction Game: A Paradox in Noncooperative Behavior and Escalation"

gancho: George Price, químico do Projeto Manhattan, criou sem formação em genética uma equação central para entender a evolução do altruísmo. Depois passou a abrigar sem-teto em casa e morreu na pobreza.
explicacao: Price teve uma carreira errante: foi químico no Projeto Manhattan, trabalhou na Bell Labs, escreveu na revista Science contra a percepção extrassensorial e foi consultor da IBM. Em 1967, depois de um câncer de tireoide, usou o dinheiro do seguro médico para recomeçar a vida em Londres. Depois de ler os trabalhos de W. D. Hamilton sobre seleção de parentesco, e sem treino em genética de populações nem em estatística, chegou à equação de Price, que descreve como a frequência de um gene muda numa população. Em 1973, assinou com John Maynard Smith um artigo pioneiro na aplicação da teoria dos jogos à biologia evolutiva, com a ideia de estratégia evolutivamente estável e o jogo do falcão e da pomba, um modelo de disputas entre animais. Em 1970, depois de uma experiência religiosa, converteu-se ao cristianismo, doou o que tinha aos pobres e passou a abrigar sem-teto e a ajudar alcoólatras, que chegaram a roubar seus pertences. Deprimido e doente, tirou a própria vida em 1975. Do meio acadêmico, só Hamilton e Maynard Smith foram à cerimônia em sua memória.

fontes.trecho: Price converted to Christianity and gave all his possessions to the poor. Struggling with a thyroid condition in conditions of great poverty, he grew increasingly depressed and committed suicide. [...] Price was a member of the Manhattan Project as a chemist looking into the characteristics of plutonium-235. [...] Later, he took a position at Bell Laboratories to work on the chemistry of transistors. [...] In 1955 and 1956, he published two papers in the journal Science criticizing the pseudoscientific claims of extrasensory perception. [...] From 1961 to 1967, Price was employed by IBM as a consultant on graphic data processing. In 1966, he was treated for thyroid cancer [...] With the money from his medical insurance, he moved to the United Kingdom to start a new life in November 1967. [...] Price had read Hamilton's 1964 papers on kin selection, and with no training in population genetics or statistics devised the Price equation, a covariance equation that generated the change in allele frequency of a population. [...] On 6 June 1970, Price had a religious experience [...] He also pioneered the application of game theory to evolutionary biology, in a co-authored 1973 paper with John Maynard Smith. [...] he dedicated the latter part of his life to helping the homeless, often inviting homeless people to live in his house. [...] He also gave up everything to help alcoholics; yet as he helped them steal his belongings, he increasingly fell into depression. [...] Price died by suicide on January 6, 1975 [...] A memorial service was held for Price in Euston. The only persons present from academia were Hamilton and Maynard Smith

The earliest presentation of a form of the Hawk–Dove game was by John Maynard Smith and George Price in their paper, "The logic of animal conflict". [...] The hawk–dove version of the game imagines two players (animals) contesting an indivisible resource
second, introducing (with John Maynard Smith) the concept of the evolutionarily stable strategy (ESS), a central concept in game theory

gancho: Os EUA já distribuíram frequências de celular por sorteio. Em 1994, um leilão inventado por teóricos dos jogos vendeu 10 licenças por 617 milhões de dólares. O formato depois rendeu mais de 200 bilhões no mundo.
explicacao: No começo, as licenças de rádio eram dadas em "concursos de beleza": as empresas tinham de argumentar por que mereciam a frequência, gastavam fortunas com lobby e o governo arrecadava pouco. Com a explosão da telefonia móvel, o Congresso americano permitiu sorteios, que também rendiam pouco e davam às operadoras redes retalhadas. Especuladores revendiam as licenças por bilhões de dólares, dinheiro que não ia para o Tesouro. Em 1993, decidiu-se leiloar. O problema é que o valor de uma frequência numa região depende das que a empresa conseguir nas outras, e quem leiloa uma por vez deixa os compradores no escuro, com medo de pagar caro demais. É a "maldição do vencedor": quem ganha costuma ser o mais otimista, e o otimismo vira prejuízo. Paul Milgrom e Robert Wilson, em parte com Preston McAfee, criaram o leilão simultâneo de múltiplas rodadas: todas as licenças são vendidas ao mesmo tempo, começando com preços baixos e permitindo lances repetidos. Na estreia, em julho de 1994, foram 47 rodadas. Só nos leilões da agência americana FCC com esse formato, foram mais de 120 bilhões de dólares entre 1994 e 2014. A dupla ganhou o Nobel de Economia de 2020.

fontes.titulo: The Prize in Economic Sciences 2020 - Popular science background
fontes.trecho: The most optimistic bidder often overestimates the common value of an auctioned object, so that ‘winning’ the auction turns out to cause a loss – the winner’s curse. [...] This was initially done through a process known as a beauty contest, in which companies had to provide arguments for why they, in particular, should receive a licence. This process meant that telecom and media companies spent huge amounts of money on lobbying. The revenue generated by the process was limited, however. [...] After pressure from the FCC, the US Congress permitted the use of lotteries for allocating frequency bands. The beauty contest was thus replaced by an entirely random allocation of licences, which likewise generated only limited income for the government. [...] national mobile operators would typically get entirely discontinuous networks with different frequency bands in different regions. [...] The market value of the licences was many billions of dollars – money that ended up in the hands of frequency speculators instead of in the US Treasury [...] Finally, in 1993, it was decided that frequency bands would be distributed using auctions. [...] Also, the value of a specific frequency band in a specific region depends on the other frequency bands owned by a specific operator. [...] To tackle these problems, Milgrom and Wilson – partly with Preston McAfee – invented an entirely new auction format, the Simultaneous Multiple Round Auction (SMRA). This auction offers all objects (radio frequency bands in different geographic areas) simultaneously. By starting with low prices and allowing repeated bids, the auction reduces the problems caused by uncertainty and the winner’s curse. When the FCC first used an SMRA in July 1994, it sold 10 licences in 47 bidding rounds for a total of 617 million dollars – objects which the American government had previously allocated practically for free. [...] The FCC’s auctions alone, using this format, have brought more than 120 billion dollars over twenty years (1994–2014) and, globally, this mechanism has generated more than 200 billion dollars from spectrum sales.

fontes.titulo: The Prize in Economic Sciences 2020 - Popular science background
fontes.trecho: The Prize in Economic Sciences 2020 [...] Paul R. Milgrom [...] Robert B. Wilson [...] “for improvements to auction theory and inventions of new auction formats”

gancho: Desde os anos 1950, os EUA distribuem recém-formados em medicina pelos hospitais com um método muito parecido com o que dois matemáticos só publicariam em 1962. A semelhança foi descoberta em 1984.
explicacao: Nos anos 1940, a disputa por estudantes de medicina levava hospitais a oferecer vagas de residência cada vez mais cedo, às vezes anos antes da formatura, com prazos curtos de resposta. A saída, no início dos anos 1950, foi uma central, o National Resident Matching Program (NRMP). Em 1962, David Gale e Lloyd Shapley publicaram, usando casamentos como exemplo, um procedimento de "aceitação adiada": um lado faz propostas, o outro guarda a melhor sem aceitar de vez e rejeita as demais, e os rejeitados tentam a próxima opção. Eles provaram que o método sempre leva a pares estáveis, em que ninguém tem motivo para desfazer o par e formar outro. Num estudo de 1984, Alvin Roth descobriu que o algoritmo da central médica era muito próximo desse. Há um detalhe: o lado que propõe sai favorecido. No NRMP, quem propunha eram os hospitais. Em 1995, Roth foi chamado para redesenhar o sistema. O novo algoritmo, com as propostas feitas pelos candidatos e capaz de acomodar casais de médicos, foi adotado em 1997 e passou a preencher mais de 20 mil vagas por ano. Shapley e Roth dividiram o Nobel de Economia de 2012.

fontes.titulo: The Prize in Economic Sciences 2012 - Popular information
fontes.trecho: In 1962, Shapley applied the idea of stability to a special case. In a short paper, joint with David Gale, he examined the case of pairwise matching [...] They used marriage as one of their illustrative examples. [...] The solution – the Gale-Shapley “deferred acceptance” algorithm – was a set of simple rules that always led straight to a stable matching. [...] Each man then looks at the different proposals he has received (if any), retains what he regards as the most attractive proposal (but defers from accepting it) and rejects the others. The women who were rejected in the first round then propose to their second-best choices [...] During the 1940s, competition for scarce medical students forced hospitals to offer residencies (internships) increasingly early, sometimes several years before graduation. [...] In order to make more offers quickly, hospitals imposed strict deadlines for responding to offers. [...] In response to these problems, a centralized “clearinghouse”, called the National Resident Matching Program (NRMP), was introduced in the early 1950s. In a paper from 1984, Alvin Roth studied the algorithm used by this clearinghouse and discovered that it was closely related to the Gale-Shapley algorithm. [...] The NRMP – where the hospitals offered positions to students – was also criticized for systematically favoring hospitals over students. Indeed, as Gale and Shapley had shown theoretically, the proposing side of the market (in this case, the hospitals) is systematically favored. In 1995, Roth was asked to help design an improved algorithm that would eliminate these problems. Along with Elliott Peranson, he formulated an algorithm, built on applicant proposals and designed to accommodate couples. The new algorithm, adopted by the NRMP in 1997, has worked well and over 20,000 positions per year have since been matched with applicants.

fontes.titulo: The Prize in Economic Sciences 2012 - Popular information
fontes.trecho: The Prize in Economic Sciences 2012 [...] This year’s Prize to Lloyd Shapley and Alvin Roth extends from abstract theory developed in the 1960s

gancho: Thomas Schelling mostrou com um modelo simples que bairros podem ficar fortemente segregados mesmo quando todos aceitam vizinhos diferentes e só querem que alguns poucos sejam parecidos consigo.
explicacao: No modelo, ninguém é intolerante: todos aceitam de bom grado morar perto de pessoas de outra cultura, religião ou cor de pele. A única exigência é ter pelo menos alguns vizinhos com as mesmas características. Quem não tem se muda para onde haja mais gente parecida. Cada mudança altera a vizinhança de outros, que por sua vez podem se mudar, e o efeito se acumula. Schelling mostrou que preferências bem fracas sobre a proporção de vizinhos semelhantes bastam para produzir padrões de moradia fortemente segregados. Ou seja, um problema social pode surgir sem que ninguém tenha preferências extremas. A ideia é um exemplo do tema que atravessa a obra dele, resumido no título do livro Micromotivos e Macrocomportamento, de 1978: o que acontece quando planos individuais se encontram no espaço social. Schelling, que também aplicou a teoria dos jogos à corrida armamentista da Guerra Fria, dividiu o Nobel de Economia de 2005 com Robert Aumann.

fontes.titulo: The Prize in Economic Sciences 2005 - Popular information
fontes.trecho: The Prize in Economic Sciences 2005 [...] Robert Aumann and Thomas Schelling have contributed to enhancing our understanding of conflict and cooperation. [...] In the mid-1950s, Thomas Schelling began to apply game-theory methods to one of the era’s most vital issues – global security and the arms race. [...] A recurring theme in Thomas Schelling’s research is: what happens when individual plans and patterns of behavior are confronted in the social arena? The title of one of his most widely read books, Micromotives and Macrobehavior (1978), reveals the overall theme. [...] Schelling formulated a simple model where he assumed that all individuals are tolerant in the sense that they willingly live in the proximity of people with a different culture, religion or skin color, but that they want to have at least a few neighbors that share their own characteristics. If not, then they move to a neighborhood where they can [...] more people like themselves. Schelling showed that even rather weak preferences regarding the share of like persons in a neighborhood can result in strongly segregated living patterns. In other words, no extreme preferences on the part of individuals are required in order for a social problem to arise.

gancho: Nos anos 1990, satélites mostraram pastos nômades da Mongólia mais conservados que os vizinhos da China e da Rússia, onde houve coletivização (e, na China, privatização). Elinor Ostrom ajudou a entender por quê.
explicacao: O argumento clássico contra os bens comuns, como pastos, pesqueiros e florestas, é simples: cada usuário pesa só o próprio ganho e ignora o dano aos outros, e o recurso acaba esgotado. A receita seria o governo regular ou privatizar. Ostrom juntou estudos de recursos comuns no mundo todo e concluiu que eles muitas vezes são surpreendentemente bem administrados pelos próprios usuários, que criam e fiscalizam suas regras. Nas estepes da Ásia, rebanhos pastam há séculos. Na Mongólia, a tradição nômade seguia quase intacta nos anos 1990. Nas áreas vizinhas, com condições parecidas, os governos impuseram coletivos estatais com moradia fixa, e a terra se degradou. No início dos anos 1980, a China tentou reverter isso privatizando boa parte dos pastos da Mongólia Interior, o que também fixou as famílias e piorou a degradação. A lição não é que a gestão comunitária sempre vence: há casos em que privatizar ou regular funciona melhor. Mas regras criadas pelos próprios usuários, e fiscalizadas por eles, tendem a ser mais respeitadas que as impostas de fora. Em 2009, Ostrom se tornou a primeira mulher a ganhar o Nobel de Economia.

fontes.titulo: The Prize in Economic Sciences 2009 - Popular information
fontes.trecho: Many natural resources, such as fish stocks, pastures, woods, lakes, and groundwater basins are managed as common property. [...] It has frequently been suggested that common ownership entails excessive resource utilization, and that it is advisable to reduce utilization either by imposing government regulations, such as taxes or quotas, or by privatizing the resource. The theoretical argument is simple: each user weighs private benefits against private costs, thereby neglecting the negative impact on others. However, based on numerous empirical studies of natural-resource management, Elinor Ostrom has concluded that common property is often surprisingly well managed. [...] It neglects the fact that users themselves can both create and enforce rules that mitigate overexploitation. [...] Scientists have studied satellite images of Mongolia and neighboring areas in China and Russia, where livestock has been feeding on large grassland areas for centuries. [...] In Mongolia, these traditions were largely intact in the mid-1990s, while neighboring areas in China and Russia – with closely similar initial conditions – had been exposed to radically different governance regimes. There, central government imposed state-owned agricultural collectives, where most users settled permanently. As a result, the land was heavily degraded in both China and Russia. In the early 1980s, in an attempt to reverse the degradation, China dissolved the People’s Communes and privatized much of the grassland of Inner Mongolia. [...] this policy encouraged permanent settlement rather than pastoral wandering, with further land degradation as a result. As satellite images clearly reveal, both socialism and privatization are associated with worse long-term outcomes than those observed in traditional group-based governance. [...] The lesson is not that user-management is always preferable to all other solutions. There are many cases in which privatization or public regulation yield better outcomes than user management. [...] Rules that are imposed from the outside or unilaterally dictated by powerful insiders have less legitimacy and are more likely to be violated. Likewise, monitoring and enforcement work better when conducted by insiders than by outsiders.
In 2009, Ostrom became the first woman to receive the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences.

gancho: No jogo do ultimato, recusar uma oferta deixa os dois sem nada, e mesmo assim ofertas baixas são recusadas. Num estudo em 15 sociedades de pequena escala, nas culturas de dar presentes, até ofertas altas eram rejeitadas.
explicacao: Um jogador recebe uma quantia e propõe como dividi-la. O outro aceita, e cada um leva sua parte, ou recusa, e ninguém leva nada. Pela teoria, o segundo deveria aceitar qualquer valor acima de zero, já que algo é melhor que nada, e o primeiro, sabendo disso, ofereceria quase nada. Desde o primeiro experimento, de Werner Güth e colegas, em 1982, as pessoas fazem outra coisa. Uma revisão de 37 estudos achou ofertas típicas em torno de 40% do total. Entre membros de um mesmo grupo social, a divisão meio a meio é comum, e ofertas abaixo de 30% costumam ser recusadas. Mesmo em rodadas únicas e anônimas, mais de 80% dos jogadores fogem do resultado previsto. Mas o padrão varia entre culturas. Numa pesquisa com 15 sociedades de pequena escala, nas culturas em que dar presentes é central, quem propunha oferecia mais, e quem recebia recusava ofertas altas com mais frequência, mesmo sem saber quem oferecia. Em outras sociedades, ofertas baixas eram esperadas e aceitas. Os autores ligaram as diferenças ao modo como dar e receber afetam o status social em cada grupo.

fontes.trecho: the best-known article is the 1982 experimental analysis of Güth, Schmittberger, and Schwarze. [...] When carried out between members of a shared social group (e.g., a village, a tribe, a nation, humanity) people offer "fair" (i.e., 50:50) splits, and offers of less than 30% are often rejected. [...] Oosterbeek et al. (2004) reviewed 37 studies and found that the first player typically offers around 40% of the "pie," [...] In one study of 15 small-scale societies, proposers in gift-giving cultures were more likely to make high offers and responders were more likely to reject high offers despite anonymity, while low offers were expected and accepted in other societies, which the authors suggested were related to the ways that giving and receiving were connected to social status in each group. [...] Since an individual who rejects a positive offer is choosing to get nothing rather than something [...] Even in anonymous one-shot settings, the economic-theory suggested outcome of minimum money transfer and acceptance is rejected by over 80% of the players.

gancho: Thomas Schelling perguntou a estudantes onde e quando encontrariam um desconhecido em Nova York, sem poder combinar nada antes. A resposta mais comum: meio-dia, na estação Grand Central.
explicacao: É um jogo de coordenação: qualquer lugar e horário serviriam, desde que os dois escolhessem o mesmo. Pela teoria, há infinitas soluções igualmente boas, e acertar seria questão de sorte. Mas as pessoas acertam com muito mais frequência do que isso faria supor, porque convergem para o que Schelling chamou de ponto focal: uma opção que se destaca para todos. Nada torna a Grand Central um ponto de encontro melhor que um bar ou uma biblioteca, mas sua tradição como lugar de encontro a deixa em evidência. Schelling testou outros casos: ao ordenar as letras A, B e C, a grande maioria escreveu "ABC". Os experimentos informais de Schelling, publicados no livro A Estratégia do Conflito, de 1960, foram depois repetidos em condições controladas, com prêmios em dinheiro, por Judith Mehta. A ideia ajuda a explicar por que normas sociais funcionam como solução para coordenar pessoas e por que é difícil mudá-las.

fontes.trecho: In game theory, a focal point (or Schelling point) is a solution that people tend to choose by default in the absence of communication in order to avoid coordination failure. The concept was introduced by the American economist Thomas Schelling in his book The Strategy of Conflict (1960). [...] to determine the time and place to meet a stranger in New York City, but without being able to communicate in person beforehand. In this coordination game, any place and time in the city could be an equilibrium solution. Schelling asked a group of students this question and found that the most common answer was "noon at (the information booth at) Grand Central Terminal". There is nothing that makes Grand Central Terminal a location with a higher payoff because people could just as easily meet at another public location, such as a bar or a library, but its tradition as a meeting place raises its salience and therefore makes it a natural "focal point". Later, Schelling's informal experiments have been replicated under controlled conditions with monetary incentives by Judith Mehta. The existence of focal points can help explain the use of social norms, including traditional gender roles, in order to ensure coordination, and why changing said norms can be difficult. [...] Head-tail game: Name "heads" or "tails". If the two players name the same, they win an award, otherwise, they get nothing. Letter order game: Give an order to letters A, B, and C. [...] For the three players, A, B, and C, in letter order game. 9 out of 12 A, 10 out of 12 B, and 14 out of 16 C wrote "ABC".

fontes.titulo: The Prize in Economic Sciences 2005 - Popular information
fontes.trecho: In his research, including classroom experiments with his students, Schelling found that coordinative solutions – which he called focal points – could be arrived at more often than predicted by theory.

gancho: No jogo da galinha, dois carros correm um contra o outro e perde quem desviar. Uma tática vencedora é arrancar o próprio volante à vista do rival: às vezes, ter menos opções é uma vantagem.
explicacao: No jogo, o melhor para cada um é que o outro ceda, e o pior de tudo é ninguém ceder. Tentando o melhor resultado, cada lado arrisca o pior. Se um dos motoristas desativa o volante de forma bem visível antes da largada, o outro fica obrigado a desviar. Thomas Schelling, Nobel de Economia de 2005, explicou por que pode ser vantajoso limitar as próprias alternativas ou piorar as próprias opções, ao pé da letra queimar as pontes. Um exemplo real é o manifestante que se algema a um objeto: nenhuma ameaça consegue fazê-lo sair, porque ele não pode sair. Na ficção, o filme Dr. Fantástico, de Stanley Kubrick, leva a ideia ao extremo com a "máquina do juízo final" soviética, que destruiria o mundo se os EUA atacassem. O filósofo Bertrand Russell comparou a política nuclear da Guerra Fria a esse jogo de jovens imprudentes e previu que, um dia, nenhum dos lados aguentaria ser chamado de "galinha". Na biologia, o mesmo jogo é chamado de falcão e pomba e modela animais disputando um recurso.

fontes.trecho: The game of chicken, also known as the hawk-dove game or snowdrift game, is a model of conflict for two players in game theory. The principle of the game is that while the ideal outcome is for one player to yield (to avoid the worst outcome if neither yields), individuals try to avoid it out of pride, not wanting to look like "chickens". [...] This yields a situation where each player, in attempting to secure their best outcome, risks the worst. [...] Bertrand Russell famously compared the game of Chicken to nuclear brinkmanship [...] This is a policy adapted from a sport that, I am told, is practiced by some youthful degenerates. [...] The moment will come when neither side can face the derisive cry of 'Chicken!' from the other side. [...] The name "hawk–dove" refers to a situation in which there is a competition for a shared resource and the contestants can choose either conciliation or conflict; this terminology is most commonly used in biology and evolutionary game theory. [...] For example, if one party were to ostentatiously disable their steering wheel just before the match, the other party would be compelled to swerve. This shows that, in some circumstances, reducing one's own options can be a good strategy. One real-world example is a protester who handcuffs themselves to an object, so that no threat can be made which would compel them to move (since they cannot move). Another example, taken from fiction, is found in Stanley Kubrick's Dr. Strangelove. In that film, the Russians sought to deter American attack by building a "doomsday machine", a device that would trigger world annihilation

fontes.titulo: The Prize in Economic Sciences 2005 - Popular information
fontes.trecho: The Prize in Economic Sciences 2005 [...] why it could be advantageous to limit one’s own alternatives or worsen one’s own options – literally to burn one’s bridges.

gancho: Num jogo, cada um escolhe um número de 0 a 100 e vence quem chegar mais perto de 2/3 da média. A lógica perfeita leva a 0, mas num concurso de jornal com 19.196 participantes o número vencedor foi 21,6.
explicacao: O raciocínio vai em degraus. Mesmo que todos chutem 100, o alvo não passa de 66 e dois terços, então não faz sentido chutar acima disso. Sabendo que ninguém passará desse valor, o alvo máximo cai de novo, e assim por diante, até que só sobra o 0, o único equilíbrio de Nash do jogo. Para chegar lá, porém, não basta ser racional: é preciso que todos saibam que todos são racionais, e que todos saibam que todos sabem, indefinidamente. Na prática, as pessoas param poucos degraus antes. Quem supõe que os outros chutam ao acaso, com média 50, aposta 33; quem dá um passo além aposta 22. O número vencedor do Politiken, em 2005, ficou perto desse segundo degrau: 21,6, com o prêmio dividido entre cinco pessoas. As evidências indicam que a maioria raciocina entre zero e três degraus, e seriam precisos cerca de 21 para chegar a 0. Até alunos de pós-graduação em economia não chutam 0. No concurso online do jornal dinamarquês Politiken, o prêmio era de 5 mil coroas. Quem jogaria 0 só faria bem se soubesse que todos os outros são perfeitamente racionais. A versão de 1981, criada por Alain Ledoux numa revista francesa de jogos, pedia números de 1 a 1 bilhão.

fontes.trecho: is a game where players simultaneously select a real number between 0 and 100, inclusive. The winner of the game is the player(s) who select a number closest to [...] of the average of numbers chosen by all players. [...] In 1981, Ledoux used this game as a tiebreaker in his French magazine Jeux et Stratégie. He asked about 4,000 readers, who reached the same number of points in previous puzzles, to state an integer between 1 and 1,000,000,000. [...] There is a unique pure strategy, Nash equilibrium. [...] The highest possible average that would occur if everyone guessed 100 is [...] 100, that is, 66 + [...] Therefore, choosing a number that lies above [...] 100 is strictly dominated for every player, and can thus be eliminated. [...] If the same group of people play the game consistently, this process of the highest possible logical answer repeatedly getting smaller will continue for each step as the logic is continually applied. [...] To achieve its Nash equilibrium of 0, this game requires all players to be perfectly rational, rationality to be common knowledge, and all players to expect everyone else to behave accordingly. Common knowledge means that every player has the same information, and they also know that everyone else knows that, and that everyone else knows that everyone else knows that, and so on, indefinitely. [...] Level 1 players would assume that everyone else was playing at level 0, responding to an assumed average of 50 in relation to naive play, and thus their guess would be 33 (2/3 of 50). At k-level 2, a player would play more sophisticatedly and assume that all other players are playing at k-level 1, so they would choose 22 (2/3 of 33). [...] It would take approximately 21 k-levels to reach 0, the Nash equilibrium of the game. [...] Evidence suggests that most people play at k-levels 0 to 3 [...] This means that perfectly rational players playing in such a game should not guess 0 unless they know that all other players are perfectly rational as well [...] It has been demonstrated that even economics graduate students do not guess 0. When performed among ordinary people it is usually found that the winner's guess is much higher than 0: [...] in a large online competition organized by the Danish newspaper Politiken. 19,196 people participated and the prize was 5000 Danish kroner.

fontes.titulo: New York Times puzzle is pure game theory
fontes.trecho: Past versions of this type of competition include one run by Danish magazine Politiken in 2005, using similar rules, in which 19,196 entrants turned out a winning value of 21.6 (the prize was shared by five people).

gancho: Num programa de TV britânico, os finalistas escolhiam em segredo "dividir" ou "roubar" o prêmio. Pesquisadores notaram que quem tocava fisicamente o rival tinha menos chance de dividir, e quem puxava o riso, mais.
explicacao: No Golden Balls, a final é uma variante do dilema do prisioneiro com dinheiro de verdade. Se os dois escolhem "Split", dividem o prêmio. Se um escolhe "Steal" e o outro "Split", quem roubou leva tudo. Se os dois roubam, ninguém ganha nada. Antes da escolha, eles podem conversar e prometer o que quiserem. Em média, os jogadores escolheram dividir em 53% das vezes. Economistas, entre eles Richard Thaler, viram que quem prometia dividir tinha mais chance de cumprir, e que a cooperação era surpreendentemente alta em quantias que seriam importantes fora dali, mas pareciam pequenas no contexto do programa. Biólogos evolutivos, entre eles Stuart West, notaram que tomar a iniciativa do contato físico, ou ser tocado, se associava a uma chance menor de dividir, e que puxar o riso se associava a uma chance maior. Outro estudo analisou as falas: quem dizia "vou dividir" cooperava mais do que quem dizia "quero dividir", "vim aqui para dividir" ou "divido se você dividir".

fontes.trecho: Each contestant is given a set of two balls, one each marked "Split" and "Steal", and must secretly choose one to indicate their intentions after looking inside to confirm which is which. The contestants may speak to each other and ask Carrott for advice before making their decision. If both choose Split, they each receive half the jackpot. If one chooses Steal and the other chooses Split, the Steal contestant wins the entire jackpot and the Split contestant leaves with nothing. If both choose Steal, neither contestant wins any money. [...] A team of economists, including Richard Thaler, has analysed the decisions of the final contestants and found, among other things, the following: Individual players on average choose split (to cooperate) 53 percent of the time. Contestants' propensity to cooperate is surprisingly high for amounts that would normally be considered consequential but look tiny in their current context [...] Contestants that promised to split were more likely to split. Two evolutionary biologists, including Stuart West, have also analysed the correlates of decisions of the final contestants [...] Contestants that initiated laughter were more likely to split. In contrast, contestants that initiated physical contact were less likely to split, and being touched was also correlated with being less likely to split. Another study focuses on whether it is possible to predict the behaviour of contestants by carefully analyzing what they say. They find that contestants who make statements that carry an element of conditionality ("I will split if you split") or implicitness ("I want to split", "I came here to split") are less likely to cooperate than contestants who make more explicit promises ("I will split"). [...] The "Split or Steal?" game element, essentially a variant of the prisoner's dilemma

gancho: Um dos algoritmos mais antigos ainda em uso, o de Euclides, que acha o maior divisor comum de dois números, foi descrito por volta de 300 a.C. Hoje é um dos passos do RSA, criptografia muito usada no comércio eletrônico.
explicacao: O algoritmo calcula o máximo divisor comum, o maior número que divide dois inteiros sem deixar resto. Ele aparece nos Elementos de Euclides, mas provavelmente não foi invenção dele: Euclides reuniu no livro resultados de matemáticos anteriores, e Eudoxo de Cnido provavelmente já o conhecia por volta de 375 a.C. Séculos depois, foi redescoberto de forma independente na Índia e na China, sobretudo para resolver equações que surgiam na astronomia e na confecção de calendários precisos. No fim do século V, o astrônomo indiano Aryabhata o chamou de "pulverizador". O método serve para simplificar frações e entra em muitos cálculos de criptografia. No RSA, muito usado no comércio eletrônico, ele ajuda a achar o número que serve para decifrar a mensagem. Em 1844, Gabriel Lamé provou que o algoritmo nunca precisa de mais passos do que cinco vezes o número de algarismos do menor dos dois números. Essa prova é vista como o começo da teoria da complexidade computacional e como a primeira aplicação prática dos números de Fibonacci: o pior caso, já estudado em 1837, acontece justamente quando os dois números são Fibonacci consecutivos.

fontes.trecho: greatest common divisor (GCD) of two integers, the largest number that divides them both without a remainder. It is named after the ancient Greek mathematician Euclid, who first described it in his Elements (c. 300 BC). It is an example of an algorithm, and is one of the oldest algorithms in common use. It can be used to reduce fractions to their simplest form, and is a part of many other number-theoretic and cryptographic calculations. [...] The algorithm was probably not discovered by Euclid, who compiled results from earlier mathematicians in his Elements. [...] The algorithm was probably known by Eudoxus of Cnidus (about 375 BC). [...] Centuries later, Euclid's algorithm was discovered independently both in India and in China, primarily to solve Diophantine equations that arose in astronomy and making accurate calendars. In the late 5th century, the Indian mathematician and astronomer Aryabhata described the algorithm as the "pulverizer" [...] This equation can be solved by the Euclidean algorithm, as described above.
